1.why: Clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing appears throughout every screen.

2.why: No italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs are used; all copy is short sentence case.

3.why: Layout is a single narrow column with large tap targets and ample whitespace, readable at mobile width.

4.why: Instructions such as “Enter the six-digit code…” are brief and use plain everyday words.

5.why: No example format, placeholder, or sample value is shown for email, phone, or verification code.

6.why: Every screen contains only one or two short sentences; no long text block must be read to continue.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control or selectable secret is offered for any code the user must handle.

8.why: No QR code or alternative to typing the verification code appears on any screen.

9.why: Standard email/tel inputs may allow browser autofill, but no explicit autocomplete attributes or password-manager affordances are visible.

10.why: Page heading states the current step and the blue primary button is the most prominent element.

11.why: Each screen asks for only a single action—sign-in fields or one verification code.

12.why: Aside from a generic log line and a vague error, the UI never plainly confirms success or states what happens next.

13.why: Retry is possible after the error, yet no resend, reveal, hide, or re-request control for codes is provided.

14.why: The message “We could not complete that request. Please try again.” does not explain the actual problem or a concrete fix.

15.why: No countdown or expiry timer is displayed, so reading and entry time appear unrestricted.
